title: Hyp Perf Baselines
objective: Build exact resident-process Sage.js/Magma/PARI/Sage performance baselines on bench-1 and the versioned competitive benchmark corpus.

handoff.summary: Built and pushed a 35-case versioned competitive corpus with resident Sage.js, Magma, PARI/GP, and optional SageMath runners; exact canonical result validation; cold/object-cold/warm/repeated-loop wall and CPU timing; MAD and RSS reporting; pinned tool provenance; and explicit unsupported cells. The clean pre-performance Linux x64 acceptance receipt at a66abc56 validates 28 rows with no exact disagreement: Sage.js 28/28, Magma 19 plus 9 explicit unsupported cells, PARI 8 plus 20 explicit unsupported cells, and explicit unavailability for standalone, Wasm, and SageMath. A separate clean current packed-local-stream acceptance receipt at 70ed9cdb records deterministic 10^4 and 10^5 digests over seven repetitions; the 10^5 median is 1.809 seconds with 97.5 MB peak RSS. Human-readable reports preserve both source SHAs and label them as pre-performance baselines, not final integrated-source acceptance.
risks: The checked receipts predate integration of the performance-lane implementations. The identical corpus, normalization, timing contract, and packed-stream digest must be rerun at the final integrated higher-genus commit before claiming after-performance acceptance.

SageMath was not installed on bench-1, so every SageMath cell is retained as explicitly unavailable rather than timed. Local SageMath API probes informed the corpus but are not acceptance-host measurements.

Magma 2.18-5 exposes only a 10 ms timing quantum in this resident interface; zero-valued internal timings are reported as below resolution and are never used to form finite performance ratios. PARI 2.18.1-alpha is pinned but not host-tuned.

Generic even-degree Magma divisor points require an independent infinity weight and g+2 v coefficients. Sage.js public Jacobian arithmetic is currently odd-degree only, so even-degree group-law cells remain explicit unsupported while local-factor, period, and analytic rows remain comparable.

The slow tier is a bounded feasibility corpus rather than an accepted quiet-host receipt. Torsion, saturation, pairing/regulator timing, the optional 10^6 stream, public lazy/materialized stream stages, and production standalone/Wasm hyperelliptic backends remain explicit follow-up gaps.

The final pnpm test:changed attempt reached unit batch 5 before the unrelated Chromium group-pack test failed to load dist/wasi-runtime.mjs with HTTP 404. Current-tree syntax, exact-corpus, architecture, and strict-baselib checks pass. The identical full native suite passed in 866.2 seconds immediately before the receipt content was committed, but its post-commit refresh hit a load-induced performance assertion (generated fmpz multiply 20.90 ms versus legacy 0.19 ms) while the shared host load was 17.7 with four unrelated compiler/Node processes saturating cores. The failed run is preserved; no current-tree native pass is claimed or fabricated, and final integration must run the exact-source full gate once on an uncontended host.
next_steps: After all implementation commits are integrated, rerun the 28-case acceptance suite and packed 10^4/10^5 local stream on a clean, quiet bench-1 checkout, preserving before and after receipts and exact digests.
Run the bounded slow-tier fixtures as diagnostic feasibility checks, then promote only demonstrated short rows into the quiet acceptance tier.
Install a pinned SageMath on bench-1 only if its acceptance-host comparison is still desired; do not substitute numbers from a different host.
Add true prepared operand batches and public lazy/materialized local-stream stages as those APIs land; retain repeated_warm_loop and cache-hit labels for the historical baseline.
